exposure: perioperative opioid use (preoperative morphine milligram equivalents, opioid prescriptions)
outcome: persistent opioid use (6 or 12 weeks after surgery)
type and amount of opioids dispensed
cohort: The study included 855 consecutive patients undergoing intermediate-to-major elective surgeries, including hip arthroplasty, prostatectomy, caesarean delivery, spinal surgery, visceral surgery, or major hand surgery, at a Swiss cantonal hospital.
finding: Only 1% of surgical patients, and 0.3% of opioid-naive patients, continued opioid use 12 weeks after intermediate-to-major elective surgery, with higher ASA scores and preoperative pain levels associated with persistent opioid use.
